 Will the Southwest Stay Cold While the Rest of the Country Warms Up?
 Jenny Lynton 2026년 11월 6일 금 오후 1:49 UTC 0 A new December temperature map forecasts a warmer than usual month for most of the country, with only one region of the Lower 48 shaded for colder than normal weather. That same area also lines up with better than usual odds of snow on Christmas morning, while the Climate Prediction Center already favors above normal temperatures across nearly the entire country for mid November.
 Which States Could Be Colder Than Normal in December?
 The map comes from The Weather Company , which published its December 2026 temperature outlook on Nov. 4, alongside a look at white Christmas odds by senior meteorologist Jonathan Erdman.
 Three states fall inside the blue, below-normal zone:
 California: the southern part of the state
 Arizona: most of the state
 New Mexico: the southwestern half of the state
 The Weather Company’s December 2026 outlook shades southern California, Arizona and southwestern New Mexico for below-normal temperatures, with the deepest warmth centered on the Upper Midwest and Great LakesThe Weather Company A gray band of near-normal temperatures wraps around that zone, covering Nevada, Utah, northern California and Texas. Florida also lands near normal.
 Where Will December Run Warmest?
 Most of the remaining country is forecast to be warmer than average. The Weather Company expects a much warmer-than-average December in the Midwest and Northeast, and the darkest shading on the map sits over Minnesota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
 The company’s September winter outlook already pointed this way, calling for winter to open warm, with the largest departures from average across the Midwest and Great Lakes.
 Do Other Forecasters See the Same Cold?
 The forecasts broadly agree on a warmer northern tier and cooler conditions across parts of the South and Southwest, but they differ on how far the colder pattern extends and over what period. AccuWeather’s winter forecast expects colder conditions across parts of the central Rockies, the Southwest and the Gulf Coast from December through February, and names Phoenix and Las Vegas among the cities where that could mean higher heating demand. However, it also forecasts a warm start to December across the Upper Midwest and Great Lakes.
 Advertisement
 Fox Weather expects the active southern storm track to keep temperatures below average across parts of the Southwest, Southern Plains and Gulf Coast over the full winter.
 Federal forecasters are more cautious. NOAA’s official seasonal outlook , issued Oct. 15, leaves much of the Southwest at equal chances of a warm, near-normal or cold season and does not favour below-normal seasonal temperatures anywhere in the Lower 48.
 Does This Change the White Christmas Odds?
 Erdman writes that, based on the six strongest El Niños since 1950, white Christmas chances look much lower than usual from the Great Lakes into the Northeast. Those are historical odds, not a forecast of snow cover for Dec. 25.
 The same comparison favours the high country of the southern Rockies, including parts of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah, where the odds of snow on the ground on Christmas morning are higher than usual.
 Could the Polar Vortex Change the Forecast?
 It could. In its November outlook , the National Weather Service Climate Prediction Center calls a November disruption of the polar vortex very rare and says its effects can last up to two months, though that is no guarantee of cold in any given state.
 Forecast guidance points to a brief reversal of the winds high above the Arctic in the second week of November. If that happens, it would come more than two weeks earlier than the November events listed in NOAA’s historical dataset, according to The Watchers . The CPC says the signal is competing with El Niño.
 The official December outlook from the CPC is due Nov. 19.
